page: Amazon Web Services r8idn.metal-96xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with dedicated Intel processors featuring 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It delivers 3072.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The bare-metal design provides direct physical access to the underlying processor and memory subsystems without virtualization overhead.

For local I/O and communication capacity, the server integrates 22800 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage alongside 600 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No dedicated GPUs are included in this configuration. The bundled local storage volume provides high-capacity scratch space directly on the host, which complements the high-throughput network interface for distributed data transfers.

From an efficiency perspective, the hardware profile aggregates massive memory capacity with extensive local NVMe storage and high network throughput on a single dedicated host. The platform represents an operational tradeoff where workloads must fully utilize the substantial memory and local storage footprint to maintain resource efficiency. Best-fit deployments include large in-memory databases, massive distributed caching tiers, real-time analytics engines, and memory-heavy ETL processing.
